..
Some brief thunderstorms were visible today as moderate wind shear 
and weak upper level support developed over the convergence zone.
This is moving out of the region so thunderstorms are no longer
expected for the islands but may be visible off the coast tonight.
Otherwise, showers are expected to remain isolated at least the next
few days with occasional patches of weak, scattered trade wind 
showers possible. Gentle winds tonight will become gentle to moderate
tomorrow and may increase slightly by the end of the week. Models 
indicate a trade wind trough may move into or just north of the 
Marianas by Friday, possibly bringing more rainfall. However, the 
location of this trough remains uncertain so isolated showers remain 
in the forecast.

Marine...
Light to gentle trade winds are expected through Tuesday night, 
becoming moderate around midweek onward. Combined seas of 5 to 7 ft 
are expected to continue decreasing slowly through Tuesday night 
before remaining steady or increasing slightly due to higher trade 
winds. There will be hazardous surf and a high risk of rip currents 
along north-facing reefs through tonight. There is also a moderate 
risk of rip currents along east- and west-facing reefs. Swells 
consist of a long period north-northwest swell from distant Typhoon 
In-fa and a smaller trade wind swell. The secondary northeast to east
trade swell looks to become dominant by late Tuesday. Lastly, 
isolated thunderstorms will be possible for western coastal waters 
before midnight.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon In-fa is located near 22.6N 141.0E based on visible imagery
at 4 PM ChST. It continues moving west at 6 mph, with a decrease in
forward speed expected to occur tonight or Tuesday. Maximum 
sustained winds of 85 mph. Typhoon force winds extend out to 45 
miles, mainly on the northern side, with tropical storm force winds 
extending outward up to 150 miles from the center. Although some 
slight strengthening is possible over the next 36 to 48 hours 
(perhaps a 5 knot increase), in general winds look to remain near 70 
knots the majority of this time, with a turn more to the northwest 
expected. Thereafter, for the latter half of the week, In-fa looks to
rapidly accelerate northeast as it gradually weakens.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Pohnpei buoy is showing the northwesterly swell from distant
Typhoon In-fa continues to affect the region. As such, a higher
northwesterly (a foot above guidance, 4 feet for swell height) was
retained at Pohnpei and Kosrae for the next 36 hours, allowing it to
become light by the middle of the week. Aside from that, the main
forecast challenge was rainfall potential and the effect high clouds
will have on temperatures the next few days. Visible imagery and
streamline analysis shows a broad, weak surface circulation has
formed north of Nukuoro in the FSM. This feature is located along the
monsoon trough that extends east from there through Kosrae, becoming
east-northeast as it passes by Majuro (just to your south), before
crossing the Date Line at 9N. The trough is expected to lift north 
and settle between 5N and 6N (between Pohnpei and Kosrae) over the 
next few days as well. However, the models show Pohnpei getting dry-
slotted after Tuesday, so we only carried scattered showers for 
tomorrow there. At Kosrae and Majuro, with the trough lingering 
nearby, look for scattered showers to occur from time to time for 
much of this week.

For our mariners, seas of 4 to 6 feet will continue through Tuesday
night at Pohnpei and Kosrae, and 3 to 5 feet at Majuro. Then, for 
the latter half of the week, seas look to decrease by a foot or so. 
Light to gentle winds will prevail through the week as well.

Western Micronesia...
A monsoon-like trough continues to produce patchy showers across the
region with convection deepening along enhanced convergence south of
the trough, concentrating scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms across open waters south of Yap and Chuuk State. Spotty
thunderstorms are seen just northwest of Palau waters, moving 
southward, so have included isolated thunderstorms into the forecast 
tonight. Low-end scattered showers persist through Tuesday night, 
meanwhile relatively drier air with precipitable water amounting to 
around 1.8 inches has moved into the Yap, with mainly dry conditions 
and periods of isolated light showers through at least Wednesday. 
Gentle to moderate trades return Wednesday night for Yap and Friday 
for Palau with the overall weather pattern remaining fairly quiet and
mainly isolated showers expected through late week. Weak winds and 
daytime heating may still bring an uptick in clouds and showers over
